description: Verify that DUT discards a UDP datagram whose Source IP Address is multicast (RFC 1122 §4.1.3.6 + §3.2.1.3 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
The Source IP of an arriving packet must identify a single host. Multicast / broadcast / unspecified are illegal source addresses (RFC 1122 §3.2.1.3) — accepting them lets attackers spoof reply destinations to anyone in a group. RFC 1122 §4.1.3.6 makes the discard mandatory.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: UDP datagram
   • src_ip = an IPv4 multicast address (e.g. 224.0.0.1)   ← key trigger
   • dst_ip = DUT IP

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester must NOT receive the datagram (UT-query confirms drop)

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT did not deliver the multicast-source UDP.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT delivered the multicast-source UDP
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue)

verdicts.Pass: DUT discarded UDP with multicast src_ip — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT received UDP with multicast src_ip
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for multicast-src discard
